title: From a cardiac CT scan to a beating heart on the website
summary: A CT scanner recorded one patient's heart 21 times across a single heartbeat. Below is every command that runs, what it reads, what it writes, and the settings it uses. Nothing here is a metaphor: each block is the literal action taken on this machine.

stages.title: Check the machine
stages.what: Confirm the GPU is reachable from inside WSL, because every later stage picks cuda:0 or silently falls back to CPU.
stages.result: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU, 6141 MiB. torch 2.14.1+cu126, cuda.is_available() True.

stages.title: Install the toolkit
stages.what: Create an isolated Python 3.12 environment and install MONAI Physio. torch goes in first on its own: torch-scatter compiles against the torch headers at build time and fails if torch is absent, which is exactly how the first attempt died.
runs: uv pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --torch-backend=cu126
uv pip install cupy-cuda12x nbconvert matplotlib
settings: CUDA wheel index: cu126, matched to the 596.36 Windows driver
CuPy present, so mesh operations run on the GPU instead of NumPy
stages.result: monai-physio 2026.9.1, MONAI 1.6.1, TotalSegmentator 2.18.0, ITK 5.4.7, VTK 9.7.1, ANTsPy 0.6.1.

stages.title: Fetch the scan
stages.what: Download the 4D sequence and split it into one 3D volume per cardiac phase. The split is what makes the frames addressable: every later stage iterates over slice_000.mha to slice_020.mha.
runs: -> ConvertImage4DTo3D splits it into slice_000.mha ... slice_020.mha
settings: Source: Jolley Lab, Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, via SlicerHeart
Reference phase for everything downstream: index 14, which is int(0.7 * 21)
stages.result: 21 phases, 512 by 391 by 218 voxels at 0.6 by 0.6 by 0.7 mm, -1024 to 3071 HU, 2.5 GB on disk.

stages.title: Find the heart
stages.what: Run TotalSegmentator's nnU-Net over the reference phase only. It returns a labelmap the same size as the CT, where each voxel holds a structure number. The chamber labels 141 to 144 are the ones the beating model is built from; the myocardium wraps them.
runs: segmenter.process(reference_image)   # downloads nnU-Net weights on first call
-> sliding-window inference on cuda:0, 3 mm fast model
writes: ~/.totalsegmentator/nnunet/  (model weights, about 2 GB on first run)
settings: Network: TotalSegmentator v2, 117 structures, fast mode at 3 mm
WithContrast variant: adjusts thresholds when the scan is contrast enhanced, which this one is
Chamber label ids: 141 left atrium, 142 left ventricle, 143 right atrium, 144 right ventricle

stages.title: Measure the motion
stages.what: For each of the other 20 phases, compute a deformation field that warps it onto the reference phase. That field is the measured displacement of the tissue, which is what turns one static segmentation into a model that moves.
settings: Greedy diffeomorphic registration on the CPU, 4 resolution levels, 30/15/7/3 iterations
Metric: normalised cross correlation, the usual choice for same-modality CT
Registration mask dilated 10 mm around the heart, so the ribs and lungs do not drag the fit

stages.title: Build the surfaces
stages.what: Convert each phase's labelmap into triangle surfaces, one mesh per anatomical structure, then halve the triangle count. A browser draws triangles; it cannot draw a voxel grid.
runs: ProcessUSDAnatomy  # assigns clinical colours per structure
settings: One mesh per structure so chambers can be toggled independently on the page

stages.title: Shrink it for the web
stages.what: Decimate further, pack all phases into one binary glTF as morph targets, and build the viewer page. The USD file is for Omniverse; a browser needs glTF.
runs: trimesh.load('*.vtp') -> decimate to a per-structure triangle budget
pack phases as morph targets -> imaging/heart/heart.glb
npm run build:viewer   # esbuild bundles the three.js viewer
settings: Triangle budget chosen so the file stays under 8 MB on a phone connection
Phase slider, chamber toggles, play and pause, prefers-reduced-motion respected
